thesis: Two commanders stand at opposite ends of one door — Brallin bills the table for every card that LEAVES your hand and Shabraz pays you for every card that ARRIVES — so the deck is a hand-refill machine whose output is entirely a function of who else is standing at those two doors when a wheel resolves.

stages.label: THIRTY-SIX LANDS, NO BASICS, AND THE MONEY FOR THE SECOND WHEEL
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six lands and zero basics, plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove, plus three Treasure makers the wheel itself is supposed to pay for. The bill is two things on one turn: a 4- or 5-mana commander AND a 3-to-6-mana wheel on top, then {4} again every turn if the wheel is Queen Kayla. Measured (goldfish_metrics, 10,000 games, seed 42, model_version 5496ad1975b1): mean available mana 4.02 at T4, 5.524 at T6, 9.392 at T10; land-drop hit rate 0.817 at T4, 0.719 at T6. Blue is what binds — 54.1% of the pips on 32 land sources against a 36-source target, on-curve 0.785 ungated (mana_analysis), and 13 of 36 lands enter tapped. THE TYPED-LAND TRAP IS THE THING A PILOT MUST KNOW. Only seven lands carry a basic land type — Glittering Massif, Hallowed Fountain, Irrigated Farmland, Raugrin Triome, Sacred Foundry, Steam Vents, Thundering Falls — and the deck runs no basics at all, while six lands read a type off the board: Glacial Fortress and Sulfur Falls enter tapped without one; Floodfarm Verge and Riverpyre Verge make their first colour (W and R) unconditionally but gate their BLUE mode on 'a Plains or an Island' / 'an Island or a Mountain', and Nimbus Maze makes only colourless without one — so all three withhold blue, the colour that binds, until a typed land is down: any of the seven for the Verges, but for Nimbus Maze one of the five with Plains; and Gleaming Bastion's W/U mode is gated on 'this land entered this turn or you control a basic land', which with zero basics in the 99 means the turn it lands and no turn after. model_treasures is OFF by declaration, so the three Treasure makers here contribute no mana to any figure above; model-coverage names Generous Plunderer DARK on treasure and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove DARK on sacrifice.

stages.label: THE TWELVE WHEELS YOU SPEND
stages.what_it_does: Nothing here starts itself: every payoff in the deck is a tax collector with nothing to tax until a hand empties and refills, which is why a wheel is the one group the declaration marks `required`. These twelve are the wheels you SPEND a card to fire; the five that wheel again and again are permanents and are filed as fuel. Read the split inside this stage before you cast one. SIX discard and therefore pay Brallin — Burning Inquiry, Khorvath's Fury, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds, Windfall and Magus of the Wheel, which sacrifices itself and needs a turn to untap first. SIX shuffle or bottom and pay him nothing — Commit // Memory, Echo of Eons, Molten Psyche, Time Reversal, Whirlpool Warrior and Winds of Change — refilling you for the Shabraz half only, and refilling the table with you. Three refill only YOU: Tolarian Winds, Whirlpool Warrior's enters-trigger, and Khorvath's Fury if you call yourself friend and the table foe. Priced from the brief, and the figures are the DECLARATION's sets rather than this stage's twelve: the 17-card wheel component is drawn in 0.990 of games, 0.949 by turn six, mean turn 1.718; the 9-card DISCARD-wheel component 0.949 and 0.811 by turn six, mean turn 2.943. No figure prices these twelve on their own.

stages.label: THE WHEELS YOU DO NOT SPEND, AND THE CARDS BETWEEN THEM
stages.what_it_does: Five permanents wheel and keep wheeling: Anje's Ravager on every attack (it must attack), Queen Kayla for {4} and a tap once a turn at sorcery speed, Arjun on every spell you cast, Jace's Archivist for {U} and a tap, Teferi's Puzzle Box on every player's draw step. THREE OF THE FIVE REFILL ONLY YOU — Ravager, Kayla and Arjun — and that is the axis this deck is being bought on: two of the three nonland cards added this round are exactly that, and branches/budget-v1/branch.json records them as the two biggest single-card gains measured on the list (+1.739 and +1.102 on damage@T8 against a stated MDE of 0.695, from an uncommitted slot sweep, not from the committed run). Arjun bottoms rather than discards, so he pays Shabraz and never Brallin. Around them sit the cards that keep the hand turning between wheels: Faithless Looting and Artist's Talent move one card at a time; Teferi's Ageless Insight doubles every draw but the first each draw step, so a seven-card refill is fourteen Shabraz triggers; Mind's Eye bills the opponents' half of a symmetric wheel at {1} a card, and the only other card in the 99 that reads an opponent DRAWING is Smothering Tithe, over in mana — Rhystic Study taxes their CASTS instead, which a wheel does not cause; Library of Leng puts what a wheel discards on top of your library instead of into the graveyard; Sorcerer Class loots two on arrival (four triggers between the pair), and its level-2 mana is spell-only and cannot pay any activation above it (deck-facts flags exactly this card).

stages.label: THE TOLLBOOTHS THAT PAY IN CARDS AND COUNTERS
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper on the value side: permanents that stand at the door and take something other than life. Shabraz is the whole draw half — a +1/+1 counter and a life for every card that arrives — and the pair's counters measure 6.74 by T6 and 38.714 by T10 (their own counters only). CADENCE is what to read here, not the count. Rielle fires ONCE on the first discard each turn and draws that many, so a seven-card wheel draws seven more and pays every per-draw tollbooth twice. Ivora takes a counter per discarded card and makes Blood on arrival. Containment Construct lets you replay a discarded card that turn; Currency Converter exiles discards and buys them back later as a Treasure or a 2/2. Curator of Mysteries pays scry 1, which is selection and not advantage. Chasm Skulker grows one counter per draw and is in the declared AIR KILL component despite having no evasion — its death tokens have islandwalk, not flying. Mindless Automaton and Jaxis are the opposite shape: you PAY mana and discard one card at a time, so they do not scale with a wheel at all. Marketback Walker turns its counters into cards only when it dies. Priced from the brief: the 6-card 'discard converted to board or cards' component is drawn in 0.932 of games, 0.713 by turn six.

stages.label: THE TOLLBOOTHS THAT PAY IN LIFE TOTALS
stages.what_it_does: Brallin is the discard half and the deck's declared clock: one damage to EACH opponent per card discarded, plus a counter, so a seven-card wheel is seven to three seats. The second per-discard source is a two-card component (Glint-Horn Buccaneer, Magmakin Artillerist) drawn in 0.660 of games and 0.347 by turn six — the lowest by-turn-six rate of any payoff group in the declaration, and the second-lowest of the twelve groups outright. The two are not the same card: Glint-Horn bills PER CARD (seven triggers off a seven-card wheel) and Magmakin bills PER EVENT ('whenever you discard one or more cards, that much damage'), one trigger of seven. Identical totals until Artist's Talent is at level 3, and stack 004 PROVES the difference: its +2 is a replacement on each noncombat damage EVENT, once per event, so a seven-card wheel reads 21 a seat off Brallin and 9 off Magmakin — a per-CARD source is taxed once per card, a per-EVENT one once per wheel. On the draw half, Psychosis Crawler and Niv-Mizzet bill every card that arrives, while Irencrag Pyromancer bills the SECOND draw each turn, which is once a turn and not once a card. READ THE FIGURE WITH ITS DEFINITION: cumulative event damage against one seat is 6.918 at T8 and 15.818 at T10, and that is the whole ping pillar — it does not close a 40-life seat on its own. It IS inside the kill rate, though: goldfish_turn.py 1899-1904 takes event damage off the same opponent_life the combat step reads and can set kill_turn, so the pings are the minor share of kill_by_turn (6.918 cumulative at T8 against 33.615 of combat on turn eight alone). Damage @T10 of 61.671 is what is dealt ON turn ten, not a running total, and it is the combat-and-arrival pillar; the discard- and draw-triggered pings are not inside it.

stages.label: KEEPING A 3/3 ON THE TABLE
stages.what_it_does: The engine is two 3/3s that cost {3}{R} and {3}{W}{U}, and every figure on this page assumes they are alive. Lightning Greaves (shroud, equip {0}) and Swiftfoot Boots (hexproof) are a two-card declared component drawn in 0.651 of games and only 0.338 by turn six — the LOWEST by-turn-six rate of any of the twelve declared groups (0.338, against the next-lowest 0.347), and the one the whole model rests on. Nezahal cannot be countered, removes your maximum hand size, and its escape hatch costs three discards, which is three more Brallin triggers paid to dodge a removal spell. The two cycling answers are different answers and the label 'a real answer' hides it: Decree of Silence cycles for {4}{U}{U} and counters a spell, while Nimble Obstructionist cycles for {2}{U} and counters only an ACTIVATED OR TRIGGERED ABILITY — it cannot answer a Swords to Plowshares or a wrath. Astral Drift is not removal either: it exiles a creature and gives it back at the beginning of the next end step, and its use here is exiling your OWN commander in response to removal, once per card cycled. The suite is also mana-starved rather than card-starved: interaction is in hand in 0.552 of games at T6 and castable in 0.073.

stages.label: THE AIR FORCE THE DRAWS BUILD
stages.what_it_does: The declaration names two kills off one ignition, and this is the DOMINANT pillar of the measured kill, not the whole of it: kill_by_turn reads ONE 40-life total that both pillars lower — goldfish_turn.py subtracts event damage from opponent_life and lets it set kill_turn (lines 1899-1904) before the combat step does the same (lines 2133-2136) — so the 0.891 below is combat plus pings. The share is what makes it the air force's figure: per-turn combat is 33.615 at T8 against 6.918 CUMULATIVE ping damage by the same turn. Every card that arrives is a 1/1 flier with haste (The Locust God) or a 1/1 Faerie on the second draw each turn (Improbable Alliance) or a foreshadow counter toward an 8/8 Kraken (Ominous Seas); every card that leaves is a 2/2 Drake for {1} (Drake Haven, on a discard OR a cycle); Shark Typhoon cycles for an X/X flier at instant speed; Vanguard Suppressor squads and draws on connect. Kefnet is indestructible and cannot attack unless you hold seven cards, which is exactly the hand a wheel leaves. Silent Hallcreeper cannot be blocked. Stromkirk Noble, Waterbender Ascension and Gossip's Talent are connect-and-grow support, and two of the three are named in the model's own blind spot list (combat_effects_not_modelled: Generous Plunderer, Gossip's Talent, Stromkirk Noble). Enduring Curiosity turns each connection back into a card, which pays Shabraz again. Measured: THE AIR KILL assembles in 0.848 of games and 0.537 by turn six, mean turn 4.975; board power 9.874 at T6 and 19.171 at T10; bodies 2.437 and 7.602; kill rate against one unopposed 40-life seat 0.209 by T6, 0.635 by T7, 0.891 by T8.

lines.note: PROVED by stack 001 (checker pass, 2 rounds, 25 citations): Windfall resolved with both commanders on the battlefield and a seven-card hand. Brallin's 'whenever you discard a card' ability triggers SEVEN times, one per card YOU discard (109.5; the opponents' twelve discards do not count); each trigger deals 1 damage to EACH opponent — 7 per seat, 21 pod-wide, every seat 40 -> 33 — and Brallin ends with seven +1/+1 counters. The discard and the draw are ONE resolution (608.2c), no player receives priority inside it, so NONE of the fourteen triggers (seven Brallin, seven Shabraz) is put on the stack until Windfall has finished resolving (603.3): Brallin is a 3/3 with no counters throughout the discard AND while the seven are drawn; then their controller orders all fourteen (603.3b). No figure prices this pair alone — the goldfish accumulates every per-discard and per-draw payoff into one series, and that series reads 15.818 cumulative event damage against ONE seat by turn ten.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. The same seven discards bill twice, but in two shapes: Brallin seven times at 1, Magmakin once at 7. The second per-discard source is the declaration's thinnest payoff component at 0.660 assembled / 0.347 by turn six, and Magmakin was added this round on judgement rather than a number — branches/budget-v1/branch.json records it 'MEASURED AT -0.134 TO -0.556 ON damage_8 AND TAKEN ANYWAY', bought as insurance against the first source eating a removal spell, which a goldfish with no removal cannot price.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. Rielle reads 'whenever you discard one or more cards for the first time each turn, draw that many' — one trigger sized to the whole wheel, so a seven-card discard draws seven MORE, and those seven pay Shabraz a second time on the same wheel. Cadence is the whole point: Rielle scales with a wheel, Mindless Automaton in the same stage does not.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. The round's direction in one arrow: Ravager discards your hand and draws three every time it attacks, refilling nobody else, so it is a Brallin payment every combat that costs neither a card nor a mana. Recorded at +1.739 on damage@T8 against a stated MDE of 0.695 in branches/budget-v1/branch.json — an uncommitted slot sweep, not the committed run, and not a measurement of this pair.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. Kayla discards the whole hand for {4} and a tap, paying Brallin for every card, then returns an artifact or creature card of mana value 1, 2 and 3 from among what she just discarded — Currency Converter at 1 and Rielle at 3 are both legal targets, so the same activation can rebuild the tollbooths it just pitched. Activate only as a sorcery, and she needs a turn to untap first, which is why she is fuel and not ignition.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. The doubler applies to every draw except the first in each draw step, so a wheel's seven arrives as fourteen and Shabraz takes fourteen counters plus fourteen life. The draw-multiplier channel is live this round and Teferi's Ageless Insight is no longer in meta.draw_not_modelled, so its effect is inside EXTRA cards drawn @T10 (beyond the draw step) of 23.017 and commander counters @T10 of 38.714 — neither figure is this card's share.

PROVED by stack 004 (checker pass, 3 rounds, 34 citations): eight triggers on the stack after a seven-card Windfall — Magmakin Artillerist's single trigger at the bottom, Brallin's seven above — with Artist's Talent at level 3. Its level-3 ability is a replacement effect (614.1a) that applies to each damage EVENT as the abilities resolve one at a time, and once per event (614.5): each Brallin trigger deals 1 + 2 = 3 to each opponent, 21 per seat over the seven, and Magmakin's one trigger deals 7 + 2 = 9 — 30 per seat, 90 pod-wide, every seat 40 -> 10. Brallin gets one counter per resolution (seven; 608.2c), unaffected by the damage change. The extra 2 is dealt by the original source, Brallin or Magmakin, never by Artist's Talent (120.2b, 120.7). That fixes the build rule the open question named, on the two sources 004 tested: a per-CARD source (Brallin) is taxed by the Talent once per card, a per-EVENT source (Magmakin) once per wheel. Glint-Horn Buccaneer is in no stack; it follows by that class rule plus its identical per-card wording, 'whenever you discard a card, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent'. It is neither cheap nor fast — {1}{R}, then {2}{R} and {2}{R} at sorcery speed — and Artist's Talent's own loot is in meta.draw_not_modelled, so none of this is priced.

PROVED by stack 002 (checker pass, round 1, 18 citations): Windfall resolved under Library of Leng with Brallin on the battlefield and a four-card hand. Leng's 'instead' is a replacement effect (614.1a) on an EFFECT's discard, and a card put into a hidden zone instead of the graveyard is still discarded (701.9c, 614.6), so all four discards count — Brallin triggers four times, 4 damage per seat, 12 pod-wide, every seat 40 -> 36, four +1/+1 counters; the four cards go on top of your library as the discard happens, in the order you choose and unrevealed (401.4), and Windfall's draw for five (opponent 2 discarded the most) draws those four straight back plus one more card from beneath them. That is why the card is a fuel arrow and not an output one: the wheel's draw pulls the cards straight back. Stack 003 (pass, round 1, 22 citations) proves the scope this note claimed — cycling Raugrin Triome under the same board, a cost paid at activation (601.2h) is not an effect (609.1), so Leng does NOT reach a cost discard — cycling is the case 003 tested, and the Triome is in the graveyard. A Blood crack and Jaxis follow by that class rule plus their oracle text, not by a stack that tested them: each one's discard sits before the colon (602.1), so it is a cost and not an effect. Brallin still triggers on the cost discard, stacks above the cycling ability and resolves first (603.3, 405.5) — 1 per seat, 3 pod-wide — before the cycle draws.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. One Blood token is a discard AND a draw off one activation: a Brallin ping and counter, an Ivora counter, a Shabraz counter and a life. The Blood channel is live this round, and its stated assumptions bound it hard — Blood made by CONNECTING in combat is read and not credited (no blockers in the model), and at most ONE token is cracked per turn, which the module itself calls an authored floor. Ivora is the deck's only Blood source.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. The partners hand each other the keyword they lack: Shabraz's '{W/U}: Target Human gains flying' and Brallin is a Human Shaman; Brallin's '{R}: Target Shark gains trample' and Shabraz is a Shark Bird. 38.714 counters by turn ten sit on two 3/3s that can each make the other connect. Both online by turn six in 0.831 of games, mean turn 5.412, never both online in 0.013.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. One of the two arguments for a symmetric wheel this deck can bank — Mind's Eye is the other: three opponents drawing seven each is 21 Smothering Tithe triggers, each a Treasure unless that player pays {2}. Entirely unpriced — model_treasures is OFF by declaration, and the flags note says so deliberately.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. The air kill's bodies are drawn, not cast: every card that arrives is a 1/1 flier with haste off The Locust God AND a counter on Shabraz, so one wheel is a board and a bigger commander at the same time. Declared AIR KILL: 0.848 assembled, 0.537 by turn six, mean turn 4.975.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. Kefnet cannot attack or block unless you have seven or more cards in hand, and a wheel is what puts seven there — an indestructible 5/5 flier that the refill itself switches on. It is the clearest case of the deck's shape: the wheel is not just fuel, it is a condition several cards read.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. Every creature that connects draws a card, and every card drawn is another Shabraz counter and another life — the air force pays the draw tollbooth back. Unpriced: Enduring Curiosity is in meta.draw_not_modelled (attack- and death-triggered draw are not modelled), so board power 9.874 at T6 does not include any cards it would have drawn.

CLAIM, no passing stack — only the Windfall + Brallin base line (stack 001), the Library of Leng line (stacks 002, 003) and the Artist's Talent line (stack 004) are proved; this arrow is the analyst's reading. A repeatable wheel is only repeatable if the mana is there every turn: Kayla asks {4} on top of whatever you cast, Jace's Archivist {U}, and Arjun asks that you cast a spell at all. Mean available mana is 5.524 at T6 and 9.392 at T10, so the second activation is affordable from about turn six and not before.

map_disagreements.why: Six cards do one job — turn a card moving into a life total going down — and they have three addresses. Brallin sits in THE THINGS THAT GROW on his +1/+1 counter; Glint-Horn Buccaneer and Magmakin Artillerist in PAID TO PITCH on their discard trigger, with Irencrag Pyromancer beside them there (deck_map.json city-0) although its trigger is a draw; Niv-Mizzet and Psychosis Crawler in THE DRAW TAX on their draw trigger — a 1 / 3 / 2 split. The map reads each card's trigger CONDITION and the engine is defined by the PAYOUT, so the deck's declared kill is invisible as a group on the map.

map_disagreements.component: THE WHEELS YOU DO NOT SPEND (the fuel stage)
map_disagreements.why: The cartographer's own finding, and I read it the same way. The five repeatable wheels have three addresses: Arjun and Queen Kayla in PAID TO PITCH, Anje's Ravager in THE DRAW TAX, Jace's Archivist and Teferi's Puzzle Box in THE WHEELS. Asymmetry and repeatability are properties of HOW a card refills, not of the words it uses, so a clustering over card text cannot express the axis the pilot buys on — and it is the axis two of this round's three nonland additions were bought on.

Brallin and Shabraz sit together in one city, correctly: both grow on card movement. Functionally they are two different machines pointed in opposite directions — Shabraz taxes the half that arrives and pays in counters, life and cards (conversion); Brallin taxes the half that leaves and pays in damage (output). One city cannot show that, and it is the single most important thing to know about piloting the deck.

Enumerated from cards.json on the word 'cycling': Astral Drift, Decree of Silence, Magmakin Artillerist, Nimble Obstructionist, Ominous Seas and Shark Typhoon in PAID TO PITCH, Curator of Mysteries in THE DRAW TAX, Glittering Massif, Irrigated Farmland and Raugrin Triome in MORE THAN MANA. Ten, up from seven before this round's land swaps. Every one is a discard AND a draw in a single activation at instant speed with no wheel involved — one Brallin trigger and one Shabraz trigger each — and the goldfish does not model cycling at all, so this entire channel is absent from every figure in this model. It has no home on the map because a cycler is clustered on what it does WHEN cycled, which is ten different things.

Both cities are the landbase, so the mana stage cuts across them — but the split is real and not arbitrary, and the round's six land swaps left it at 20/16. THE PAIRS is fixed colour pairs; Checked card by card: MORE THAN MANA holds all six lands that charge life per tap and all eight any-colour sources, including the three that pay BOTH commanders. It does NOT hold every land with a non-mana ability — Thundering Falls surveils on arrival and sits in THE PAIRS — so the city's own gloss is one card wider than the membership. What neither city expresses is the dependency that actually decides whether a land works here: the seven lands that carry a basic land type (Plains, Island or Mountain) in a deck with zero basics, which is what Glacial Fortress, Sulfur Falls, Floodfarm Verge, Nimbus Maze and Riverpyre Verge read — while Gleaming Bastion reads the Basic SUPERTYPE, which none of the seven has.

open_questions.question: Cracking one Blood token: is the discard (a cost) a Brallin and an Ivora trigger, and is the draw a Shabraz trigger, from the single activation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Blood is the newest model channel and the only card that feeds it is Ivora. If one token pays three triggers, the deck is under-built on an axis it already reads; if the cost-discard does not trigger, the Blood channel contributes only the draw.

open_questions.question: Confirm the partner keyword grants are legal: Shabraz's '{W/U}: Target Human gains flying' targeting Brallin (Human Shaman), and Brallin's '{R}: Target Shark gains trample' targeting Shabraz (Shark Bird).
open_questions.why_it_matters: 38.714 commander counters by turn ten sit on two bodies that can each give the other the keyword it lacks; it is the difference between a big blocker and a kill. Cheap to settle and it underwrites the output-to-conversion line.

open_questions.question: Stack 003 settled the Brallin half: a cycling cost's discard triggers Brallin and his trigger resolves before the cycle draws. Still open: is the cycle's draw a Shabraz trigger — and does Drake Haven's 'whenever you cycle or discard' see it once or twice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Ten cards in the 99 cycle, three of them lands added this round, and the goldfish models none of it. If cycling pays both commanders, the deck has an instant-speed second engine that no figure in this model counts.

open_questions.question: Is the deck under-built on Blood? Ivora is the only Blood source in the 99; the channel exists and is measured at one card. Sweep the Blood makers available in the identity against the current list.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A Blood token is the cheapest single object that pays BOTH commanders from one activation. If the channel moves damage@T8 on a one-card sample, a second and third source is a cheap, in-identity direction; if it does not, the Ivora slot is judged on her counters alone. Worth fixing while the sweep runs: goldfish_turn keeps `blood_by_turn` and `artifact_sacs_by_turn` per game and goldfish_metrics publishes neither, so nobody can read how many tokens this deck made or cracked.

open_questions.question: What does the deck lose by giving three opponents a fresh seven every wheel? Six of this stage's twelve one-shot wheels are symmetric, and the model prices the tax on their refill while explicitly not pricing the cost — it has no opponent turn and no opponent board.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot's own position is that an asymmetric wheel is strictly better unless it buys a discount or another ability, and that a symmetric wheel's DISRUPTION (shuffling graveyards, breaking a stored hand) is real and every metric is blind to it. Both halves of that are unmeasured, and the whole direction of the last two rounds turns on it.

open_questions.question: mana_analysis.json credits Gleaming Bastion, Floodfarm Verge, Nimbus Maze and Riverpyre Verge as unconditional blue sources and lists none of them in sources.gated, although each one's blue mode is gated on a basic land or a Plains/Island/Mountain on the battlefield and the 99 holds zero basics and seven typed lands. Is the U figure (32 land sources, on-curve 0.785 ungated) an upper bound by four sources, and should land_colors(card, pool=...) read these pool-dependent gates the way it already reads a fetchland?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The mana stage's binding colour is priced on a source count that includes four lands which cannot make blue on most boards this deck presents. A land_colors / mana-analysis code fix, not a model change; this model already reads the gates from the oracle text and the artifact does not.

findings.note: This is the inference the gate cannot make, so all six steps and final_state were read. It is not co-presence: the Talent's 'instead' modifies the very damage event Brallin's trigger produces (step 2: 608.2c then 120.4b then 614.6), and it is re-evaluated per resolution (step 4, 614.1) with one opportunity per event (614.5). final_state.damage_by_source on every seat reads Brallin 21 / Magmakin 9 / Artist's Talent 0, life 10, seven counters, 10/10. The stack's positives are read as positives (damage dealt, counters placed), not as an absence. The board does not contradict the claim (the radagast Garenbrig shape): the Talent is stipulated at level 3 from an earlier turn with its level abilities off the stack, the line leans on no mana, and mana_available is untouched from scenario to final_state. The eight-triggers premise is a scenario stipulation whose Brallin half stack 001 proved and whose Magmakin half step 5 proves on 603.2c, so nothing in the line rests on an untested premise.

The extension to Glint-Horn needs two premises from cards.json, not from the stack: its trigger reads 'Whenever you discard a card, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent' — the same per-card wording stack 001 resolved for Brallin (603.2c, seven occurrences in one event) — and that damage is noncombat from a source you control. True by rule plus oracle text, so no flow is asserted that the cited stack does not establish, and this is not a fail condition; the line's own via is Talent + Brallin and that flow is proved in full. It is the same attribution point as the Leng finding last round, which the engineer accepted in notes[-2] ('Ivora, Rielle, Glint-Horn Buccaneer and Magmakin Artillerist follow by the same rule ... and no stack tested them'); this round's notes[-1] drops that caveat. The fix is a phrase in the note, e.g. 'Glint-Horn Buccaneer, whose trigger reads the same per-card wording, follows by the same rule and was not on 004's board.' Expected rebuttal: the rule is class-level and oracle text supplies the only extra premise — I would accept that if the note says so in those words. Mechanically checkable in principle (a PROVED line's note naming a 99-card absent from every cited stack's scenario) but, as last round, it needs a fleet measurement first because notes routinely name neighbours for context.
